charts.annotation: The four-segment split starts FY2026, after Construction was divested; FY2025's Light Building Products figure is shown where disclosed comparably, the rest only from FY2026.

charts.title: Segment EBIT
charts.annotation: Profitability by segment matters more than revenue mix here: Distribution is the largest revenue segment but the thinnest EBIT margin of the four.

charts.title: Significant Items (One-Off Charges)
charts.annotation: Negative values are charges against reported earnings; EBITDABeforeSignificant and EBITContinuingBeforeSignificant above add these back.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Fletcher Building Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Fletcher Building Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Fletcher Building Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Fletcher Building Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Fletcher Building Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Fletcher Building Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Fletcher Building Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Fletcher Building Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Fletcher Building Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue mix
segmentRevenue.content:
Revenue split across Fletcher Building's four continuing segments: Light Building Products, Heavy Building Materials, Distribution and Residential & Development.

For Fletcher Building Limited: the group divested its Construction division in FY2026 after years of Australian construction losses, so this mix reflects the business as it now stands, not the historical blended Revenue line above. Distribution is the largest segment by revenue.

What to watch:

  • Whether Residential & Development revenue holds up through the NZ housing cycle
  • Distribution's revenue share versus its EBIT share (see the EBIT chart) — volume without margin

segmentEbit.title: Segment EBIT
segmentEbit.content:
Operating profit (EBIT) for the same four continuing segments, shown separately because revenue share and profit share diverge by segment.

For Fletcher Building Limited: Light Building Products (higher-margin manufactured products) typically earns a fatter EBIT share than its revenue share, while Distribution (a lower-margin merchant/trade business) earns less profit per dollar of revenue than its size suggests. This is the more useful view than revenue mix alone for a company that just exited its loss-making Construction arm.

What to watch:

  • Any segment's EBIT margin (EBIT / segment revenue) trending down
  • Residential & Development EBIT, which is directly exposed to New Zealand housing completions and settlement timing

significantItems.title: Significant items (one-off charges)
significantItems.content:
Significant items are the one-off charges and provisions management strips out to get from statutory EBIT/EBITDA to the "before significant items" figures shown elsewhere on this dashboard — legacy asbestos and leaky-building liabilities, Iplex Pro-fit pipe defect provisions, and losses on the now-divested Australian construction business.

For Fletcher Building Limited: this line has been negative in nearly every year on record, including FY2025's -$644m (Iplex Pro-fit plus Australian construction losses) and FY2024's -$333m. "Significant" and "one-off" are the label, not the pattern — treat this as a recurring cost of doing business, not noise to exclude from valuation.

What to watch:

  • Whether charges keep recurring post-Construction-divestiture (FY2026 was a comparatively modest -$41m)
  • Which segment or legacy liability is driving each year's charge
